item.title: California voters reject billionaire wealth tax, CBS News projects
item.description: Voters in California have rejected a tax on the state's wealthiest residents, CBS News projects, following a campaign that has split traditional allies and shattered spending records for a tax-related measure in California.

item.title: These House and Senate midterm races don't have winners yet
item.description: Democrats won sizable House and Senate majorities in the 2026 midterm elections, but the exact margins are unclear because some races haven't been projected yet. Here's where the results stand.

item.title: Where the Iran war stands as Trump says he sees "no reason" to escalate attacks
item.description: President Trump on Monday met with Qatar's prime minister to discuss strategies for a new ceasefire with Iran. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Trump defends Hegseth as Massie moves for impeachment
item.description: GOP Rep. Thomas Massie on Monday introduced new articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. CBS News' Taurean Small and Olivia Rinaldi have more on that and all the top news from Washington.

item.title: Rep.-elect Scott Wiener says Trump is "not connected to reality" on Iran, economy, immigration
item.description: President Trump held a surprise press briefing at the White House on Monday featuring UFC CEO Dana White. Democratic Representative-elect Scott Wiener of California joins CBS News with reaction.

item.title: Mike Johnson on midterm results: "The people have spoken"
item.description: Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters Monday that "there's not much more that any of us could've done" after massive GOP losses to Democrats in last week's midterm elections.

item.title: U.S. measles cases more than doubled in 2026, compared with all of 2025
item.description: More than twice as many U.S. measles cases were counted this year as there were in all of 2025. This week, experts for the Pan American Health Organization will rule on the country's elimination status. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder has more.

item.title: Trump says Jensen Huang told him he had "no idea she was a spy" amid Chinese intel allegations
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of operating as a spy for China. President Trump told reporters Monday that Huang said he had no idea about the accusations. Henry Chandonnet, a senior reporter for Business Insider, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Trump said deportation policies may have been too tough, then he promoted Stephen Miller
item.description: Just hours after telling 60 Minutes that his immigration policies may have been too tough at times, President Trump announced that he had promoted Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration's immigration strategy, to the role of White House chief of staff. CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over Chinese spy concerns
item.description: The board of Nvidia said it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

item.title: FDA warns of rare vision-loss side effect from GLP-1 drugs
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration is adding a new warning about possible rare cases of vision loss reported with GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic, Wegovy and other brands.

item.title: Texas school honors retired custodian by naming school after her
item.description: A school district in Aubrey, Texas, was named to honor a janitor who went above and beyond. Most called Marilyn Hampton a "school helper" because of how far she went out of her way for students. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: GLP-1s must now include warning for potential increased risk of vision loss, FDA announces
item.description: The FDA announced that GLP-1 weight loss drugs will now include warning labels indicating a potential increased risk of vision loss.

item.title: Fraternity suspended after video shows men on fire
item.description: A fraternity at Ohio State University has been temporarily suspended while authorities investigate a video that appears to show two people engulfed in flames.

item.title: Ohio State frat suspended after video shows 2 students with sweatpants on fire
item.description: Warning: Disturbing video. Ohio State put Sigma Alpha Epsilon on an immediate, temporary suspension "pending a full investigation" after an off-campus video showed two Ohio State students with their sweatpants on fire, trying to smother the flames. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Breaking down Republicans' losses in the 2026 midterms
item.description: With votes still coming in for last week's midterm elections, some Republicans are barely hanging on in districts that voted for President Trump by about 10 to 12 points in 2024. Kyle Kondik, managing editor of Sabato's Crystal Ball, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sex assault
item.description: Disgraced British television personality and Hollywood actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to prison for raping a woman in 2009 and sexually assaulting three others.

item.title: Cruise ship entertainer falls overboard, rescued at least 9 hours later by fishermen
item.description: A cruise ship entertainer is alive after falling overboard and being stranded for hours last week off the coast of Southern California. Carter Evans has the story.

item.title: Massie introduces Hegseth impeachment articles, teeing up vote
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie on Monday introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war against Iran without congressional authorization.

item.title: Judge calls Russell Brand a "sexual predator" in sentencing
item.description: British actor and comedian Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 and a half years in prison on Monday for raping a woman in 2009 and sexually assaulting three others. Holly Williams reports.

item.title: 2 planes taking off in LA nearly collide, officials say
item.description: Officials say two planes taking off from Los Angeles early Saturday morning almost collided. Kris Van Cleave has more details.

item.title: Nvidia shares drop amid CEO's alleged Chinese spy affair
item.description: Shares of Nvidia, the world's top AI chipmaker, fell more than 4% on Monday, wiping out about $200 billion in stock market value. The company's CEO admitted to an affair with a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a former data center executive suspected of spying for China. Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: Details on impeachment articles against Pete Hegseth
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, filed articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday. Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Inside Byron Donalds' successful campaign for Florida governor
item.description: Last week, Byron Donalds won Florida's gubernatorial race, setting him up to be the state's first ever Black governor. Brad Herold, senior adviser to Byron Donalds' campaign, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Judge dismisses Dolly Parton's estate's lawsuit against her nephew
item.description: The details of the resolution between Dolly Parton's estate and her nephew, Bryan Seaver, were not immediately known.

item.title: 11/9: CBS Evening News
item.description: Secret Service arrests two men near the White House; articles of impeachment were introduced against Pete Hegseth.

item.title: Trump admin. proposes stricter unemployment work search rules
item.description: Under a proposed federal rule, Americans seeking unemployment aid would have to conduct more job searches each week.

item.title: 11/9: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump holds press briefing alongside Dana White; Lawmakers return to Capitol Hill for lame duck session.

item.title: Trump told 60 Minutes to expect post-midterm firings
item.description: President Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff just hours after he told 60 Minutes that he'd be shaking up his team.

item.title: What AI could mean for the next generation of workers
item.description: AI is changing many of the tasks traditionally handled by entry-level workers. Tech executive Clara Shih discusses what that could mean for the next generation of employees Sunday on 60 Minutes.
